There are several open-source large-language models (LLMs) that are available for research and development:
1. GPT-3 (Generative Pretrained Transformer 3): This is a language model developed by OpenAl, a collaborative AI research group. It is based on the Transformer architecture and is trained on a large corpus of text data.
2. BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers): This is a language model developed by Google and released as an open-source model by the company. It is based on the Transformer architecture and is pre-trained on a large corpus of text data.
3. ELECTRA (Efficient Large-scale Transformer Models for Offline English Language Understanding and Sentiment Analysis): This is a language model developed by Google and released as an open-source model by the company. It is based on the Transformer architecture and is pre-trained on a large corpus of text data.
4. XLNet (eXtreme Large Language Model): This is a language model developed by Facebook AI and released as an open-source model by the company. It is based on the Transformer architecture and is pre-trained on a large corpus of text data.
5. DistilBERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers with Sub-Samples): This is a language model developed by Google and released as an open-source model by the company. It is based on the Transformer architecture and uses a sub-sampled version of the BERT model to achieve higher efficiency and lower computational requirements.
These LLMs can be used in a variety of applications, such as language translation, text generation, sentiment analysis, and question-answering.
